dod_intent_evidence: DIU Prototype OT award up to $99M (Nov 2025, businesswire/Breaking Defense) followed by a contract expansion with OUSD(A&S) (Feb 19, 2026, own news page) explicitly framed as a transition from prototype to production usage.
score_evidence: "Data that Drives Overmatch" / "Thousands of Data Sources. One Unified Platform." -> lab_language_intensity

Four feature areas (Budget Intelligence, Market Landscapes, Data Modules, pipeline building) described in detail with zero mention of ATO, FedRAMP, CMMC, or data-handling controls despite ingesting DoD budget/program/contract data -> deployment_awareness_absence

"empowers companies, government agencies, and investors to deliver better technology to the warfighter" is the pack's only warfighter/operator reference; no training, CONOPS, or field-feedback language anywhere -> operator_absence

8 open roles are all sales/GTM or generalist engineering (Account Executive x2, Product Manager, VP of Engineering, Senior Engineer, two data/research analysts) with zero security/compliance/ISSO posting -> hiring_profile_skew

"Obviant Awarded Contract Expansion with OUSW(A&S)...marks an important transition from a Defense Innovation Unit prototype OT awarded in 2025" -- prototype to production-adjacent expansion in ~3 months, run by a 21-person team -> stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: The platform ingests 'thousands of structured and unstructured sources' of DoD budget, program, and contract data with no visible ATO, FedRAMP authorization, or CMMC level mentioned anywhere in the pack.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A data platform marketed directly to 'government agencies' needs to clear an accreditation bar before broad government rollout -- this is exactly the kind of compliance gap that stalls an OT-to-production-contract transition after the prototype money is spent.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company messaging is entirely feature/value-prop focused (decision advantage, unified platform) and hasn't surfaced the accreditation story publicly, which is common pre-ATO.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Obviant is a unified defense acquisition data platform created by synthesizing thousands of structured and unstructured sources"

blind_spots.blind_spot: Obviant markets to 'all sides of the market' -- companies, government agencies, AND investors -- as simultaneous customers of the same platform, with no mention of how competitively sensitive acquisition intelligence is segregated between competing defense contractors.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If Prime A and Prime B are both customers pulling market-landscape and opportunity data from the same unified platform, the data-segregation and access-control architecture is a real technical and trust problem -- unaddressed, it becomes a blocker the moment a serious government customer's security office asks about it.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The 'serve everyone' positioning is a growth strategy that predates the harder multi-tenancy security conversation a broader government rollout will force.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "We're on a mission to equip all sides of the market with the tools they need to execute effectively"

blind_spots.blind_spot: Hiring is entirely commercial GTM and generalist engineering (two Account Executive roles, Product Manager, VP of Engineering, Senior Engineer) with no security/compliance/ISSO role posted, at the exact moment the company is expanding from a DIU prototype OT into an OUSD(A&S) production contract.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Security and compliance hiring typically has to precede, not follow, a scale-up in government usage -- absence of that role at this specific inflection point is the hiring-profile version of the same fielding gap.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: 21-person team still prioritizing revenue growth (two AE roles) and core product build (VP Eng, Senior Eng) over compliance infrastructure.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "Account Executive - Government" / "VP of Engineering" / "Senior Engineer" (open roles)

opener_hook: Obviant's DIU OT just expanded into an OUSD(A&S) contract in about three months -- does the platform have a FedRAMP ATO yet?
what_they_do: Runs a unified data-intelligence SaaS platform that synthesizes thousands of DoD budget, program, and acquisition data sources into dashboards for defense companies, program offices, and investors.
